title: Rust: Option Combinators
description: Master Rust's Option type with combinators like map, and_then, and unwrap_or.

steps.title: map on Option
steps.description: Create `Some(5)` and `None`. Use `.map(|x| x * 2)` on both. Print the results.
hints: `.map` transforms the inner value if present.

verification.failureMessage: Print map results for Some(5) and None.

steps.title: and_then (flatMap)
steps.description: Write `safe_reciprocal(x: f64) -> Option<f64>` that returns None if x == 0. Use `.and_then()` to chain: `parse("2") → safe_reciprocal`. Print results for "2" and "0".
hints: `safe_reciprocal(x)` returns `if x == 0.0 { None } else { Some(1.0 / x) }`

verification.failureMessage: Chain safe_reciprocal after Some(2.0) and Some(0.0).

steps.title: unwrap_or and unwrap_or_else
steps.description: Use `.unwrap_or(0)` and `.unwrap_or_else(|| { println!("computing default..."); 42 })` on `None` and `Some(10)`. Print the unwrapped values.
hints: `.unwrap_or_else(fn)` calls the closure only if None (lazy).

verification.failureMessage: Use unwrap_or and unwrap_or_else to get values from Options.

steps.title: Filter Option
steps.description: Create an option `Some(42)`. Use `.filter(|x| *x > 50)` and `.filter(|x| *x < 50)`. Print both results.
hints: `.filter(predicate)` returns `Some(value)` if predicate is true, else `None`.

steps.title: Chain Multiple Combinators
steps.description: Write a function `process(x: f64) -> Option<String>` that formats x as string with 2 decimals, but only if x is positive. Chain: parse string → ensure positive → format. Test with "3.14159" and "-1.0".

verification.failureMessage: Chain parse → filter → map and print results.
